description: Fetches raw market price data including OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) for equities across different markets (US, China A-share, etc.).
Fetches core company fundamentals and financial statements, including company profiles, income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.
Fetches derived financial analytics, ratios, valuation metrics, risk metrics, analyst estimates, price targets, ownership activity, and ESG data for company analysis.
Fetches macroeconomic indicators and economic data such as GDP, inflation, unemployment, treasury yields, and other economic time series from sources like FRED.
Fetches news articles, social media posts, and discussions from various sources including financial news APIs, Reddit, and other social platforms for sentiment analysis and market sentiment tracking.
Fetches regulatory filings and official documents from regulatory bodies such as SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, etc.) for US-listed companies, including automatic conversion to structured formats.

Handles local data processing and file format conversion tasks. Includes generic tabular-to-Qlib conversion (import_data) and PDF-to-structured-JSON parsing (mineru_pdf_to_json) for downstream quant workflows. Not used for fetching raw market/macro/news data or training models.

Calculate the technical indicators of stock market data, evaluate factor performance/backtest metrics, and analyze text sentiment. Generates technical indicators, factor metrics (trend/momentum/volatility/candlestick, IC/IR, win rate), backtest performance metrics (returns, Sharpe, drawdown), and text-based sentiment scores. Not intended for training tasks, raw data acquisition, or custom ML feature engineering beyond the provided indicator, backtest & sentiment library.

Trains and manages quant models and benchmark experiments (XGBoost/LightGBM/GRU/LSTM/Transformer/AlphaSAGE, etc.). Not for ad-hoc indicator calculation or raw data crawling; requires prepared datasets and YAML/config-driven workflows.
Direct inference on time series using pre-trained models (LSTM/Transformer/Autoformer/Informer). No training or data acquisition; needs prepared time-series inputs with time/value columns.

Executes web search and knowledge-graph queries (Google/SerpAPI, Tavily, Wikipedia), and also lists available Qlib benchmark models for internal model selection. Not a general web crawler; unsuitable for structured financial datasets or restricted/private sources.
Fetches data from alternative markets including cryptocurrencies, forex (foreign exchange), and commodities. Provides market prices, rates, and trading data for non-equity financial instruments.

Generates professional PDF reports by combining LLM analysis with data visualizations. Reads CSV/JSON data files, generates financial charts using mplfinance, combines LLM JSON analysis with chart images using Jinja2 templates, and renders final PDF reports using WeasyPrint.
